intro: At B2 you wrote reviews with strengths, weaknesses and a recommendation; at C1 you checked whether evidence really supports a claim; and in C2 rhetoric you learnt to persuade honestly. Now you'll put it all together in a **critical review** of a book, a study, a film or a policy: a short summary, an evaluation built on clear criteria and real evidence, and a verdict the reader can trust. Warm-up: think of a film or book everyone praised that you found disappointing. Why exactly?
teachingNotes: Recap the chain in one line, don't re-teach: b2-reviews-articles (a four-part review: hook, short description without spoilers, strengths and weaknesses with specific examples, a recommendation that says who it's for; Although + weakness, then the main opinion), c1-reading-complex (does the evidence support the claim? sample size and who was asked, correlation vs causation, what's missing, bias), c2-rhetoric (persuade with evidence, ethos through fairness to the other side, no manipulation). This lesson is the WRITTEN critical review (ulasan kritis) at C2: a magazine book or film review, a review of a study for a course or a journal, an internal review of a policy for a ministry, NGO or company. 'Critical' means 'carefully judged', not 'negative': Indonesian 'kritik' is often heard as criticism only, so say this explicitly. Indonesian school 'resensi' (identitas buku, sinopsis, keunggulan, kelemahan, penutup) has a similar shape, but there the sinopsis is often the longest part; in an English critical review the evaluation is the heart.

Objective write-a-balanced. Five moves: context (what it is, who made it, where it fits) → brief summary (what it says or does, no judgement yet, no spoilers for fiction) → strengths → weaknesses → overall judgement and who it's for. The order of strengths and weaknesses can vary (some reviewers lead with the weaknesses, or organise by criterion): accept any order that is clearly signposted and balanced, but always context first and verdict last. Proportion: the summary is short (about a third at most); most of the review evaluates. Balance means both sides are weighed with evidence, not that they get equal space or that the verdict must be neutral: a review can be mostly positive or mostly negative and still be balanced.

Objective evaluate-with-evidence. Make criteria explicit: a study → the sample (who and how many), the method (how the data were collected, was there a comparison group?), whether the conclusions follow from the data; a film → script, acting, pacing (also visuals, sound); a novel → characters, plot, style; non-fiction → research, argument, clarity; a policy → cost, fairness (who pays, who benefits), evidence (has it been tested?). Judge a work against its own aims too (don't fault a light comedy for not being profound). Evidence: a specific scene, chapter or figure; quotes kept short (a phrase woven into the sentence, from the invented work); comparisons with similar works (Unlike most …, Compared with …); concessions (While/Although + clause, …; Admittedly, … / Granted, … as a separate sentence or with but; Despite / For all + noun). Precise evaluative vocabulary on a scale: groundbreaking, compelling, persuasive (arguments), thought-provoking, nuanced / uneven / laboured (forced, the effort shows; US labored), unconvincing, superficial, flawed (a serious fault, often in method), with modifiers (largely persuasive, deeply flawed, at times laboured). Avoid good, bad, interesting, nice, boring.

Objective justified-verdict. The verdict goes back to the criteria, is clear, and is hedged only where the evidence is mixed (largely, on balance, despite its flaws, a … but … phrase where the second word carries the final weight). Not sitting on the fence: 'It has good and bad points' / 'It depends on the reader' are not verdicts. Recommend for a specific reader: essential reading/viewing for …, will reward …, best suited to …, of limited interest to …. Star ratings (★★★★☆, common in newspapers and on film sites) are a quick signal, but the words must justify them and match them; academic and policy reviews use reasoned verdicts, no stars.

The node lists no commonErrors, so watch for these Indonesian habits: a review that only summarises (sinopsis-style, judgement in one closing line); polite praise without evaluation ('a very interesting and useful book; congratulations to the author', 'semoga bermanfaat'); netizen-style harshness without evidence ('trash', 'the worst film ever'); vague words, especially 'interesting' from 'menarik'; *Despite + clause ('Despite the second half drags' → Although the second half drags / Despite its slow second half); 'Admittedly' joined to the next clause with only a comma; overclaiming ('a masterpiece everyone must read'); a verdict that doesn't follow from the body. Spelling: laboured (BrE) / labored (AmE); film (BrE) / movie (AmE): accept both.

Limits and testing: everything reviewed is invented (Hujan di Braga, a film by Adi Pranata; The Lantern Keepers, a novel; studies of four-day weeks and online learning; Bandung and Surabaya city policies); never quote or name real books, films, studies or critics beyond genres. Don't teach citation styles, statistics or formal peer review. At C2 many evaluative choices are matters of style: accept any precise, well-supported judgement; only mark clear faults (summary instead of evaluation, a vague word where a precise one is asked for, no evidence, a fence-sitting or unjustified verdict, a broken concession). When the learner writes a review paragraph, give feedback in this order: are the criteria clear? is each judgement backed by a specific example? is the summary short? is the verdict clear and linked to the criteria? then ONE concrete improvement.

keyPoints.title: A balanced critical review: five moves in proportion
keyPoints.explanation: A critical review judges a work carefully: 'critical' means carefully judged, not negative. Five moves: context (what it is, who made it) → a brief summary → strengths → weaknesses → an overall judgement and who it's for. Keep the summary short (about a third at most): most of the review evaluates. Balanced means both sides are weighed with evidence, not that the verdict has to be neutral.

examples.en: Hujan di Braga, the second feature by director Adi Pranata, is a quiet family drama set in Bandung.
examples.id: Hujan di Braga, film panjang kedua sutradara Adi Pranata, adalah drama keluarga yang tenang berlatar Bandung. (konteks)

examples.en: The script is the film's great strength: Laras's grief emerges through small, telling details rather than speeches.
examples.id: Naskahnya adalah kekuatan utama film ini: duka Laras muncul lewat detail-detail kecil yang bermakna, bukan lewat pidato. (kelebihan)

id.title: Ulasan kritis yang berimbang: lima langkah dengan proporsi yang pas
id.explanation: Ulasan kritis menilai sebuah karya dengan cermat: 'critical' artinya dinilai dengan cermat, bukan negatif. Lima langkah: konteks (karya apa, siapa pembuatnya) → ringkasan singkat → kelebihan → kekurangan → penilaian akhir dan untuk siapa karya itu cocok. Buat ringkasannya pendek (paling banyak sekitar sepertiga): sebagian besar ulasan berisi penilaian. Berimbang artinya kedua sisi ditimbang dengan bukti, bukan berarti penilaian akhirnya harus netral.

keyPoints.title: Evaluate with criteria, evidence and precise words
keyPoints.explanation: Say what you are judging: a study on its sample, method and whether the conclusions follow; a film on its script, acting and pacing; a policy on its cost, fairness and evidence. Back every judgement with evidence: a specific example, a short quote, a comparison with similar works, and a fair concession (While …, / Admittedly, …). Use precise words on a scale (groundbreaking, compelling, thought-provoking, uneven, laboured, unconvincing, superficial, flawed), not good, bad or interesting.

examples.en: Sari Wulandari is compelling as Laras: in the hospital scene she barely speaks, yet her silence carries the film.
examples.id: Sari Wulandari memukau sebagai Laras: di adegan rumah sakit dia hampir tidak bicara, tapi diamnya menghidupkan film itu. (penilaian + contoh spesifik)

examples.en: Admittedly, the second half drags: three long scenes repeat the same argument.
examples.id: Harus diakui, paruh keduanya bertele-tele: tiga adegan panjang mengulang pertengkaran yang sama. (pengakuan + bukti)

examples.en: Unlike earlier studies of remote work, which relied on surveys alone, this one tracks actual output for a year.
examples.id: Berbeda dengan penelitian sebelumnya tentang kerja jarak jauh, yang hanya mengandalkan survei, penelitian ini melacak hasil kerja yang sebenarnya selama setahun. (perbandingan)

id.title: Menilai dengan kriteria, bukti dan kata yang tepat
id.explanation: Sebutkan apa yang kamu nilai: penelitian dari sampel, metode, dan apakah kesimpulannya mengikuti dari data; film dari naskah, akting dan tempo cerita; kebijakan dari biaya, keadilan dan bukti. Dukung setiap penilaian dengan bukti: contoh spesifik, kutipan singkat, perbandingan dengan karya serupa, dan pengakuan yang adil (While …, / Admittedly, …). Pakai kata yang tepat sesuai tingkatannya (groundbreaking, compelling, thought-provoking, uneven, laboured, unconvincing, superficial, flawed), bukan good, bad atau interesting.

keyPoints.title: A clear, justified verdict
keyPoints.explanation: End with a verdict that goes back to your criteria. Hedge where the evidence is mixed (largely persuasive, on balance, despite its flaws), but don't sit on the fence: 'it has good and bad points' is not a verdict. Say who it's for: essential reading for …, of limited interest to …. Star ratings are a quick signal; your reasons are what make the verdict trustworthy, and they must match the stars.

examples.en: Largely persuasive, though its sample is small, this is essential reading for HR managers in Indonesian startups.
examples.id: Sebagian besar meyakinkan, walaupun sampelnya kecil, ini bacaan wajib bagi manajer SDM di startup Indonesia.

examples.en: For all its slow patches, this is a moving, intelligent drama, though viewers who want a fast plot may lose patience.
examples.id: Meski ada bagian-bagian yang lambat, ini drama yang menyentuh dan cerdas, walaupun penonton yang ingin alur cepat mungkin akan kehilangan kesabaran.

id.title: Penilaian akhir yang jelas dan beralasan
id.explanation: Tutup dengan penilaian akhir (verdict) yang kembali ke kriteriamu. Perhalus kalau buktinya memang campur aduk (largely persuasive, on balance, despite its flaws), tapi jangan main aman di tengah: 'ada kelebihan dan kekurangannya' bukan penilaian akhir. Sebutkan untuk siapa karya itu: essential reading for … (bacaan wajib bagi …), of limited interest to … (kurang menarik bagi …). Rating bintang hanya sinyal cepat; alasanmulah yang membuat penilaianmu bisa dipercaya, dan alasan itu harus cocok dengan jumlah bintangnya.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina's 900-word review of an invented study spends 600 words summarising it and 300 evaluating it. About how much of a critical review should the summary take: about a third, about a half, or most of it?
guidedPractice.hint: The evaluation is the main part of a critical review.

guidedPractice.prompt: Replace the vague word with ONE precise adjective that means 'it makes you think deeply': 'The documentary is interesting: I kept questioning my own shopping habits for days.'
Complete the concession with ONE word: '___, the second half drags; but the final twenty minutes are superb.'
guidedPractice.hint: An adverb meaning 'I have to accept that …', followed by a comma.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which ending is a reasoned verdict, A or B? A: '★★★★☆' B: 'Four stars: a gripping script let down only by an unconvincing final scene.' Write A or B.
guidedPractice.hint: Which one gives reasons linked to criteria?

independentPractice.prompt: Put the five moves of a critical review in the order taught in this lesson. Write the letters: A weaknesses, B context, C overall judgement, D brief summary, E strengths.
independentPractice.hint: Start with what the work is; end with who it's for.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete the recommendation with ONE word: 'This is ___ reading for anyone who teaches English in Indonesia.'
independentPractice.hint: A strong word: you really should read it.

independentPractice.prompt: A reviewer writes 'The study is bad.' The real problem is a serious fault in its method. Which word is more precise: flawed or uneven?
independentPractice.hint: Uneven means some parts are good and some are weak.

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan is reviewing an invented study of online learning in Surabaya. One of his sentences: 'The authors interviewed 40 secondary-school teachers in three Surabaya schools over one semester.' Which part of the review is this sentence from? Choose from: summary, strengths, weaknesses, verdict. Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: summary (it describes what the study did, with no judgement: no evaluative word, no praise or criticism). 'context' = 50 (not in the list, and context says what the work is; this sentence describes its method). 'strengths' or 'weaknesses' = 0 (40 teachers is neither praised nor criticised here). 'verdict' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi's review of an invented novel, The Lantern Keepers, has four parts: what the book is and who wrote it, a short summary of the plot, three paragraphs on what the novel does well, and a final recommendation. Which part is missing for a balanced review? Choose from: context, summary, strengths, weaknesses, verdict. Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: weaknesses (context, summary, strengths and a verdict are there; nothing weighs what the novel does less well, so the review is one-sided). 'criticism' or 'limitations' = 100 (same idea). 'verdict' = 20 (he has a final recommendation). 'context', 'summary' or 'strengths' = 0.

assessment.prompt: A reviewer describes the humour in an invented comedy film: every joke is set up slowly, explained, then repeated, so it feels forced and heavy rather than funny. Which word is the most precise evaluation? Choose from: groundbreaking, laboured, thought-provoking, compelling. Write the word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: laboured (US spelling labored = 100): forced, you can see the effort, it doesn't flow (laboured humour, a laboured joke). 'groundbreaking', 'thought-provoking' or 'compelling' = 0 (all positive; the description is clearly negative). A word not in the list such as 'heavy-handed' = 60 (precise and negative, but not from the list); 'unfunny' = 40; 'bad' or 'boring' = 10 (vague).

assessment.prompt: An invented study surveyed 12 employees at one Jakarta startup for two weeks, then claimed that a four-day week 'will work for every company in Indonesia'. Which word best describes the study? Choose from: groundbreaking, uneven, flawed, compelling. Write the word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: flawed (a serious fault in the method: a tiny sample from one company over two weeks, and a conclusion that doesn't follow from the data). 'uneven' = 20 (uneven means some parts are strong and others weak; here the basic design is the problem). 'groundbreaking' or 'compelling' = 0 (positive). A precise word not in the list such as 'unconvincing' = 60.

assessment.prompt: Complete the sentence from a practice book review with ONE word: '___ its middle chapters are slow, the final fifty pages of the novel are among the most moving I have read this year.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: although / while / though / whilst (a concession followed by a clause; 'even though' = 100). 'Despite' or 'in spite of' = 30 (the right idea, but they need a noun or -ing: Despite its slow middle chapters …). 'Admittedly' = 20 (the right idea, but it needs its own sentence or 'but': Admittedly, its middle chapters are slow, but …). 'But', 'However' or 'Because' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Dr. Wulan reviews an invented Bandung city policy: a Rp 50,000 monthly waste fee that every household pays, rich or poor. Her criteria are cost, fairness and evidence. She found it cheap to run and supported by good evidence from a pilot in two districts, but it takes a much bigger share of a poor family's income. Which is the best verdict? A: 'Overall, the policy has some good points and some bad points.' B: 'A low-cost, well-evidenced policy that the council should keep, with a lower fee for low-income households.' C: 'This disastrous policy will ruin poor families and should be scrapped at once.' Write A, B or C.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (clear, linked to all three criteria: cost, evidence and the fairness problem, with a specific recommendation). A = 0 (sits on the fence: no judgement, no link to the criteria). C = 0 (ignores her findings on cost and evidence and exaggerates the fairness problem).

assessment.prompt: Complete the end of a practice review of an invented guide to Indonesian tax law with ONE word: 'Essential reading for accountants and small-business owners; of ___ interest to general readers.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: limited (the fixed phrase 'of limited interest to'; 'little', 'marginal' or 'minor' = 100). 'no' = 60 (grammatical, but much harsher than the evidence suggests). 'some' = 40 (grammatical, but the semicolon sets up a contrast with 'essential'). 'great', 'much' or 'special' = 0 (they contradict the contrast).

blocks.text: **Three Indonesian habits to adjust.** (1) **Only summarising**: four paragraphs of plot, then one line, *Overall the book is very good.* (2) **Polite praise without evaluation**: *A very interesting and useful book. Congratulations to the author!* (and no *Semoga bermanfaat* at the end). Out of respect we often avoid saying what doesn't work, but an English reader then can't trust the praise either. (3) **Netizen-style harshness**: *This film is trash, the worst ever.* A severe judgement is fine in a critical review, but it needs evidence and measured words: *The script is unconvincing: the main characters change their minds without any reason we can see.*

id.text: **Tiga kebiasaan orang Indonesia yang perlu disesuaikan.** (1) **Hanya meringkas**: empat paragraf alur cerita, lalu satu baris, *Overall the book is very good.* (2) **Pujian sopan tanpa penilaian**: *A very interesting and useful book. Congratulations to the author!* (dan jangan ditutup dengan *Semoga bermanfaat*). Karena sungkan, kita sering menghindari menyebut apa yang kurang berhasil, padahal pembaca berbahasa Inggris jadi tidak bisa memercayai pujiannya juga. (3) **Pedas ala netizen**: *This film is trash, the worst ever.* Penilaian yang keras boleh saja dalam ulasan kritis, tapi harus ada buktinya dan kata-katanya terukur: *The script is unconvincing: the main characters change their minds without any reason we can see.*

blocks.prompt: Sari's 900-word review of an invented novel has 650 words of plot summary and 250 of evaluation. What should she change?
options: Nothing: a detailed summary shows she read the book carefully.
Shorten the summary and expand the evaluation.
Cut the evaluation, so that the review stays neutral.
blocks.explain: In a critical review the summary is the short part (about a third at most) and the evaluation is the main part. A long summary doesn't prove careful reading: careful judgement does. And a review with no evaluation isn't neutral, it simply isn't a review.

id.prompt: Ulasan Sari sepanjang 900 kata tentang sebuah novel rekaan berisi 650 kata ringkasan alur dan 250 kata penilaian. Apa yang sebaiknya dia ubah?
id.explain: Dalam ulasan kritis, ringkasan adalah bagian yang pendek (paling banyak sekitar sepertiga) dan penilaian adalah bagian utama. Ringkasan yang panjang tidak membuktikan dia membaca dengan cermat: penilaian yang cermatlah buktinya. Dan ulasan tanpa penilaian bukan netral, tapi memang bukan ulasan.
options: Tidak perlu diubah: ringkasan terperinci menunjukkan ia membaca dengan teliti.
Persingkat ringkasan dan perluas penilaiannya.
Hapus penilaian agar ulasannya tetap netral.

id.title: Dari ulasan biasa ke ulasan kritis

material.title: Criteria: say what you are judging

blocks.text:
**Criteria** (*kriteria penilaian*, singular *criterion*) are the standards you judge a work by. Make them explicit, either in one sentence near the start (*I will judge the policy on three criteria: cost, fairness and evidence.*) or by giving each one its own paragraph. Typical criteria:
- **a study**: the **sample** (*sampel*: who was studied and how many), the **method** (*metode*: how the data were collected; was there a comparison group?), and **whether the conclusions follow** from the data. This is the C1 question again: does the evidence support the claim? Remember correlation vs causation.
- **a film or series**: the **script** (*naskah*), the **acting** (*akting*), the **pacing** (*tempo cerita*: too slow, too rushed, or just right), plus visuals and sound.
- **a novel**: characters, plot, style. **Non-fiction**: research, argument, clarity.
- **a policy**: **cost** (*biaya*), **fairness** (*keadilan*: who pays and who benefits?) and **evidence** (*bukti*: has it been tested, and did it work?).

**Judge a work against its own aims.** A light comedy shouldn't be criticised for not being philosophical, and a short guide for beginners shouldn't be criticised for leaving out advanced theory. Ask first: what is it trying to do, and for whom? Then: how well does it do it?

id.text:
**Criteria** (*kriteria penilaian*, bentuk tunggalnya *criterion*) adalah standar yang kamu pakai untuk menilai sebuah karya. Sebutkan dengan jelas, entah dalam satu kalimat di awal (*I will judge the policy on three criteria: cost, fairness and evidence.*) atau dengan memberi satu paragraf untuk setiap kriteria. Kriteria yang umum:
- **penelitian (study)**: **sample** (*sampel*: siapa yang diteliti dan berapa banyak), **method** (*metode*: bagaimana datanya dikumpulkan; adakah kelompok pembanding?), dan **apakah kesimpulannya mengikuti** dari data. Ini pertanyaan C1 lagi: apakah buktinya mendukung klaimnya? Ingat korelasi vs sebab-akibat.
- **film atau serial**: **script** (*naskah*), **acting** (*akting*), **pacing** (*tempo cerita*: terlalu lambat, terlalu terburu-buru, atau pas), ditambah visual dan suara.
- **novel**: tokoh, alur, gaya bahasa. **Nonfiksi**: riset, argumen, kejelasan.
- **kebijakan (policy)**: **cost** (*biaya*), **fairness** (*keadilan*: siapa yang membayar dan siapa yang diuntungkan?) dan **evidence** (*bukti*: sudah diuji belum, dan berhasil tidak?).

**Nilai karya berdasarkan tujuannya sendiri.** Komedi ringan tidak pantas dikritik karena tidak filosofis, dan panduan singkat untuk pemula tidak pantas dikritik karena tidak membahas teori tingkat lanjut. Tanyakan dulu: karya ini mau melakukan apa, dan untuk siapa? Lalu: seberapa baik ia melakukannya?

blocks.prompt: A reviewer writes: 'The authors claim that the training programme reduced staff turnover, but they never compare it with a group of staff who had no training.' Which criterion is she judging?
options: the pacing
the method
the acting
blocks.explain: She is judging how the study was designed: without a comparison group, nobody can tell whether turnover fell because of the training or for another reason. Pacing and acting are criteria for films and series, not studies.

id.prompt: Seorang pengulas menulis: 'The authors claim that the training programme reduced staff turnover, but they never compare it with a group of staff who had no training.' Kriteria apa yang sedang dia nilai?
id.explain: Dia menilai rancangan penelitiannya: tanpa kelompok pembanding, tidak ada yang bisa tahu apakah tingkat karyawan keluar turun karena pelatihan itu atau karena alasan lain. Pacing dan acting adalah kriteria untuk film dan serial, bukan penelitian.
options: alur dan tempo penyajian
metode
akting

id.title: Kriteria: sebutkan apa yang kamu nilai

material.title: Evidence: examples, short quotes, comparisons, concessions

blocks.text:
A judgement without evidence is only an opinion. Four tools turn it into an evaluation:

**1. A specific example.** Point to the scene, the chapter, the table or the figure. *The acting is strong* → *In the hospital scene, Sari Wulandari barely speaks, yet her silence carries the film.*

**2. A short quote** (*kutipan singkat*): a few words from the work, woven into your own sentence, in quotation marks. *The narrator calls Jakarta 'a city that never finishes being built', and the novel's best chapters live up to that image.* (A practice quote from an invented novel.) Quote to show something, not to fill space: a phrase, rarely more than a sentence.

**3. A comparison** (*perbandingan*) with similar works: *Unlike most Indonesian family dramas, which end in a big reconciliation, this one leaves the conflict open.* / *Compared with earlier studies of the four-day week, its sample is tiny.*

**4. A concession** (*pengakuan*): admit the other side before your main point. It shows fairness, which builds trust (ethos, from C2 rhetoric). Watch the grammar:
- **While / Although / Though + clause**, main clause: *While the second half drags, the film remains compelling.*
- **Admittedly, / Granted,** + a full sentence, then *but* or a new sentence: *Admittedly, the sample is small, but the method is careful.*
- **Despite / For all + noun**: *Despite its slow second half, …* / *For all its flaws, …*

As at B2, the **main clause carries your real opinion**: *Although the acting is superb, the script is unconvincing* is overall negative.

id.text:
Penilaian tanpa bukti hanyalah pendapat. Empat alat mengubahnya menjadi evaluasi:

**1. Contoh spesifik.** Tunjuk adegannya, babnya, tabelnya atau angkanya. *The acting is strong* → *In the hospital scene, Sari Wulandari barely speaks, yet her silence carries the film.*

**2. Kutipan singkat** (*short quote*): beberapa kata dari karya itu, dirangkai ke dalam kalimatmu sendiri, dengan tanda kutip. *The narrator calls Jakarta 'a city that never finishes being built', and the novel's best chapters live up to that image.* (Kutipan latihan dari novel rekaan.) Kutip untuk menunjukkan sesuatu, bukan untuk memenuhi halaman: satu frasa, jarang lebih dari satu kalimat.

**3. Perbandingan** (*comparison*) dengan karya serupa: *Unlike most Indonesian family dramas, which end in a big reconciliation, this one leaves the conflict open.* / *Compared with earlier studies of the four-day week, its sample is tiny.*

**4. Pengakuan** (*concession*): akui sisi lain sebelum poin utamamu. Ini menunjukkan sikap adil, yang membangun kepercayaan (ethos, dari retorika C2). Perhatikan tata bahasanya:
- **While / Although / Though + klausa** (bagian kalimat yang punya subjek dan kata kerja), lalu klausa utama: *While the second half drags, the film remains compelling.*
- **Admittedly, / Granted,** + kalimat lengkap, lalu *but* atau kalimat baru: *Admittedly, the sample is small, but the method is careful.*
- **Despite / For all + kata benda**: *Despite its slow second half, …* / *For all its flaws, …*

Seperti di B2, **klausa utama membawa pendapatmu yang sebenarnya**: *Although the acting is superb, the script is unconvincing* secara keseluruhan bernada negatif.

rows.en: Unlike earlier studies of remote work, which relied on surveys alone, this one tracks actual output for a year.

blocks.text: **Despite is followed by a noun or -ing, never a full clause.** ✗ *Despite the second half drags, …* ✓ *Despite its slow second half, …* / *Despite dragging in the second half, …* / *Although the second half drags, …* Indonesian *meskipun* works with both, which is why this mix-up is so common. And **Admittedly** starts its own sentence: ✗ *Admittedly the sample is small, the method is careful.* ✓ *Admittedly, the sample is small, but the method is careful.*

id.text: **Despite diikuti kata benda atau bentuk -ing, tidak pernah klausa lengkap.** ✗ *Despite the second half drags, …* ✓ *Despite its slow second half, …* / *Despite dragging in the second half, …* / *Although the second half drags, …* Kata *meskipun* dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa dipakai untuk keduanya, makanya kekeliruan ini sangat sering terjadi. Dan **Admittedly** membuka kalimatnya sendiri: ✗ *Admittedly the sample is small, the method is careful.* ✓ *Admittedly, the sample is small, but the method is careful.*

blocks.prompt: Which sentence uses a concession correctly?
options: Despite the ending is rushed, the series is gripping.
Although the ending is rushed, the series remains gripping.
Admittedly the ending is rushed, the series remains gripping.
blocks.explain: Although + a full clause (the ending is rushed), then the main clause with the writer's opinion. Despite needs a noun (Despite its rushed ending, …). Admittedly needs its own sentence or 'but': two full clauses joined only by a comma are a mistake in formal writing.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang memakai pengakuan (concession) dengan benar?
id.explain: Although + klausa lengkap (the ending is rushed), lalu klausa utama dengan pendapat penulis. Despite butuh kata benda (Despite its rushed ending, …). Admittedly butuh kalimatnya sendiri atau 'but': dua klausa lengkap yang hanya disambung koma adalah kesalahan dalam tulisan formal.

material.title: Precise evaluative words on a scale

blocks.text:
**Good**, **bad**, **nice** and **interesting** tell the reader almost nothing. *Interesting* is the big trap: Indonesian *menarik* appears in nearly every school *resensi*, but in an English review it says only 'I noticed it'. Choose a word that says **exactly what works or fails**. From strong praise to strong criticism:
- **groundbreaking**: completely new; it changes how a field works (*a groundbreaking study*). Keep it for work that really is the first of its kind.
- **compelling**: so strong you have to keep watching, reading or believing (*a compelling performance*, *compelling evidence*).
- **persuasive**: an argument or case that convinces (*a persuasive case for …*). Used for arguments, not for stories.
- **thought-provoking**: it makes you think deeply and question things (*a thought-provoking documentary*).
- **nuanced**: it shows the fine differences, not just black and white (*a nuanced portrait of a family*).
- **uneven**: the quality goes up and down: some parts strong, others weak (*an uneven second season*).
- **laboured** (US *labored*): forced; you can see the effort and it doesn't flow (*laboured jokes*, *a laboured metaphor*).
- **unconvincing**: you don't believe it (*an unconvincing ending*, *an unconvincing argument*).
- **superficial**: shallow; it only touches the surface (*a superficial analysis*).
- **flawed**: it has a serious fault, often in the method or the reasoning (*a flawed study*, *deeply flawed*).

**Adjust the strength** with a modifier: *largely persuasive*, *at times laboured*, *slightly uneven*, *deeply flawed*. A precise word plus an example is the core of every evaluation.

id.text:
**Good**, **bad**, **nice** dan **interesting** hampir tidak memberi tahu pembaca apa-apa. *Interesting* adalah jebakan terbesar: kata *menarik* muncul di hampir setiap *resensi* sekolah, tapi dalam ulasan berbahasa Inggris kata itu hanya berarti 'saya memperhatikannya'. Pilih kata yang menyebutkan **persis apa yang berhasil atau gagal**. Dari pujian yang kuat sampai kritik yang keras:
- **groundbreaking**: benar-benar baru; mengubah cara kerja suatu bidang (*a groundbreaking study*). Simpan kata ini untuk karya yang memang pertama di jenisnya.
- **compelling**: begitu kuat sampai kamu harus terus menonton, membaca atau percaya (*a compelling performance*, *compelling evidence*).
- **persuasive**: argumen yang meyakinkan (*a persuasive case for …*). Dipakai untuk argumen, bukan untuk cerita.
- **thought-provoking**: membuatmu berpikir dalam dan mempertanyakan banyak hal (*a thought-provoking documentary*).
- **nuanced**: memperlihatkan perbedaan-perbedaan halus, bukan hanya hitam-putih (*a nuanced portrait of a family*).
- **uneven**: kualitasnya naik turun: sebagian kuat, sebagian lemah (*an uneven second season*).
- **laboured** (ejaan Amerika *labored*): dipaksakan; usahanya terlihat dan tidak mengalir (*laboured jokes*, *a laboured metaphor*).
- **unconvincing**: tidak meyakinkan, kamu tidak percaya (*an unconvincing ending*, *an unconvincing argument*).
- **superficial**: dangkal; hanya menyentuh permukaan (*a superficial analysis*).
- **flawed**: punya cacat serius, sering pada metode atau penalarannya (*a flawed study*, *deeply flawed*).

**Atur kekuatannya** dengan kata penguat atau pelunak: *largely persuasive* (sebagian besar meyakinkan), *at times laboured* (kadang dipaksakan), *slightly uneven* (agak naik turun), *deeply flawed* (cacat sangat serius). Kata yang tepat ditambah contoh adalah inti dari setiap penilaian.

rows.en: The book is interesting. → The book offers a nuanced portrait of three generations of a Medan family.
rows.id: Buku itu menarik. → Buku itu menyajikan potret yang bernuansa tentang tiga generasi sebuah keluarga di Medan.

rows.id: Argumen untuk makan siang gratis di sekolah sebagian besar meyakinkan, walaupun perkiraan biayanya kabur.

blocks.prompt: A 300-page book on Indonesia's economy gives only two pages to the informal sector, where most Indonesians work. Which word best describes its treatment of the informal sector?
options: groundbreaking
superficial
compelling
blocks.explain: Two pages on the sector where most people work only touches the surface: superficial. Groundbreaking and compelling are strong praise, and nothing in the description deserves praise.

id.prompt: Sebuah buku setebal 300 halaman tentang ekonomi Indonesia hanya memberi dua halaman untuk sektor informal, padahal di sanalah sebagian besar orang Indonesia bekerja. Kata mana yang paling tepat menggambarkan cara buku itu membahas sektor informal?
id.explain: Dua halaman tentang sektor tempat sebagian besar orang bekerja hanya menyentuh permukaan: superficial (dangkal). Groundbreaking dan compelling adalah pujian yang kuat, dan tidak ada yang layak dipuji dalam deskripsi itu.

id.title: Kata penilaian yang tepat, dari pujian sampai kritik

blocks.text:
The **verdict** (*penilaian akhir*) is the sentence your reader remembers. Three things make it **justified** (*beralasan*):

**1. It goes back to your criteria.** If you judged a policy on cost, fairness and evidence, the verdict should mention them, not suddenly praise its 'beautiful logo'.

**2. It's clear, and hedged only where the evidence is mixed.** Hedging (*memperhalus klaim*, from C1) is honest when the picture really is mixed: *largely persuasive*, *on balance*, *despite its flaws*. But **sitting on the fence** (*main aman di tengah*) is not a verdict: ✗ *It has good points and bad points.* ✗ *Whether you like it depends on you.* In an *X but Y* phrase, the second word carries the final weight: *uneven but rewarding* is a recommendation; *rewarding but uneven* is a warning. Avoid the opposite fault too: overclaiming (*a masterpiece that everyone must read*) when your own body paragraphs found problems.

**3. It says who it's for.** A specific reader helps far more than *I recommend it*:
- *essential reading / viewing for …* (wajib dibaca / ditonton oleh …)
- *will reward readers who …* / *best suited to …*
- *of limited interest to …* (kurang menarik bagi …)
- *newcomers to the topic may prefer …*

**Star ratings** (★★★★☆) are common in newspapers, on film sites and in app stores. They're a quick signal, but your **words** have to justify them and **match** them: four stars on top of a review that is mostly criticism confuses the reader. Academic reviews and policy reviews use reasoned verdicts with no stars at all.

id.text:
**Verdict** (*penilaian akhir*) adalah kalimat yang diingat pembacamu. Tiga hal membuatnya **justified** (*beralasan*):

**1. Kembali ke kriteriamu.** Kalau kamu menilai sebuah kebijakan dari biaya, keadilan dan bukti, penilaian akhirnya harus menyebut ketiganya, bukan tiba-tiba memuji 'logonya yang cantik'.

**2. Jelas, dan diperhalus hanya kalau buktinya memang campur aduk.** Memperhalus klaim (*hedging*, dari C1) itu jujur kalau gambarannya memang campur aduk: *largely persuasive*, *on balance*, *despite its flaws*. Tapi **main aman di tengah** (*sitting on the fence*) bukan penilaian akhir: ✗ *It has good points and bad points.* ✗ *Whether you like it depends on you.* Dalam frasa *X but Y*, kata kedua membawa bobot terakhir: *uneven but rewarding* adalah rekomendasi; *rewarding but uneven* adalah peringatan. Hindari juga kesalahan sebaliknya: berlebihan (*a masterpiece that everyone must read*) padahal paragraf-paragrafmu sendiri menemukan masalah.

**3. Menyebutkan untuk siapa.** Pembaca yang spesifik jauh lebih membantu daripada *I recommend it*:
- *essential reading / viewing for …* (wajib dibaca / ditonton oleh …)
- *will reward readers who …* (akan memuaskan pembaca yang …) / *best suited to …* (paling cocok untuk …)
- *of limited interest to …* (kurang menarik bagi …)
- *newcomers to the topic may prefer …* (pemula di topik ini mungkin lebih cocok dengan …)

**Rating bintang** (★★★★☆) umum di koran, situs film dan toko aplikasi. Bintang adalah sinyal cepat, tapi **kata-katamu** harus membenarkannya dan **cocok** dengannya: empat bintang di atas ulasan yang isinya kebanyakan kritik membuat pembaca bingung. Ulasan akademik dan tinjauan kebijakan memakai penilaian akhir yang beralasan, tanpa bintang sama sekali.

rows.en: On balance, the four-day week study is the most careful yet, and essential reading for HR teams, though its findings may not apply outside Jakarta.
rows.id: Secara keseluruhan, penelitian tentang empat hari kerja seminggu itu yang paling cermat sejauh ini, dan wajib dibaca tim SDM, walaupun temuannya mungkin tidak berlaku di luar Jakarta.

blocks.text: **End with the verdict, not with a courtesy.** Indonesian reviews and reports often close with *Semoga bermanfaat*, thanks to the author, or an apology for any shortcomings in the review. In English, those lines weaken the ending: the last sentence should be your judgement and who the work is for.

id.text: **Tutup dengan penilaian akhir, bukan basa-basi.** Ulasan dan laporan berbahasa Indonesia sering ditutup dengan *Semoga bermanfaat*, ucapan terima kasih kepada penulis, atau permohonan maaf atas kekurangan ulasan. Dalam bahasa Inggris, kalimat-kalimat itu melemahkan penutup: kalimat terakhir harus berisi penilaianmu dan untuk siapa karya itu.

blocks.prompt: Dimas reviewed an invented study of a reading app on three criteria: sample, method, conclusions. He found a large sample and a careful method, but conclusions that go further than the data. Which verdict is justified?
options: Overall, the study has strengths and weaknesses, so readers should decide for themselves.
A large, carefully designed study whose conclusions overreach: trust its data, but read its claims with caution.
A groundbreaking study that proves reading apps work for every child in Indonesia.
blocks.explain: It goes back to all three criteria (large sample, careful method, conclusions that overreach), is clear, and tells the reader what to do with the study. The first sits on the fence; the third ignores his own finding that the conclusions go too far.

id.prompt: Dimas mengulas penelitian rekaan tentang aplikasi membaca dengan tiga kriteria: sampel, metode, kesimpulan. Dia menemukan sampelnya besar dan metodenya cermat, tapi kesimpulannya melampaui data. Penilaian akhir mana yang beralasan?
id.explain: Kalimat itu kembali ke ketiga kriteria (sampel besar, metode cermat, kesimpulan yang berlebihan), jelas, dan memberi tahu pembaca harus bagaimana menyikapi penelitian itu. Pilihan pertama main aman di tengah; pilihan ketiga mengabaikan temuannya sendiri bahwa kesimpulannya terlalu jauh.

resources.note: A clear guide to book reviews as arguments: focus on evaluation rather than summary, judge a book against its own aims, weigh strengths and weaknesses with evidence and say who would benefit from reading it. Written for American university students.

id.note: Panduan yang jelas tentang ulasan buku sebagai argumen: fokus pada penilaian, bukan ringkasan, nilai buku berdasarkan tujuannya sendiri, timbang kelebihan dan kekurangan dengan bukti, dan sebutkan siapa yang akan terbantu membacanya. Ditulis untuk mahasiswa di Amerika.

id.intro: Di B2 kamu menulis ulasan dengan kelebihan, kekurangan dan rekomendasi; di C1 kamu memeriksa apakah bukti benar-benar mendukung sebuah klaim; dan di retorika C2 kamu belajar membujuk dengan jujur. Sekarang kamu akan menggabungkan semuanya dalam **ulasan kritis** (critical review) tentang buku, penelitian, film atau kebijakan: ringkasan singkat, penilaian yang dibangun di atas kriteria yang jelas dan bukti nyata, dan penilaian akhir yang bisa dipercaya pembaca. Pemanasan: ingat-ingat film atau buku yang dipuji semua orang tapi mengecewakan buatmu. Persisnya kenapa?

assessment.cr-1: Pak Hasan sedang mengulas penelitian rekaan tentang pembelajaran daring di Surabaya. Salah satu kalimatnya: 'The authors interviewed 40 secondary-school teachers in three Surabaya schools over one semester.' Kalimat ini berasal dari bagian mana dalam ulasannya? Pilih dari: summary, strengths, weaknesses, verdict. Tulis satu kata.
assessment.cr-2: Ulasan Budi tentang novel rekaan The Lantern Keepers punya empat bagian: buku apa itu dan siapa penulisnya, ringkasan singkat alurnya, tiga paragraf tentang apa yang berhasil dari novel itu, dan rekomendasi penutup. Bagian mana yang hilang supaya ulasannya berimbang? Pilih dari: context, summary, strengths, weaknesses, verdict. Tulis satu kata.
assessment.cr-3: Seorang pengulas menggambarkan humor dalam sebuah film komedi rekaan: setiap lelucon dibangun pelan-pelan, dijelaskan, lalu diulang, sehingga terasa dipaksakan dan berat, bukan lucu. Kata mana penilaian yang paling tepat? Pilih dari: groundbreaking, laboured, thought-provoking, compelling. Tulis katanya.
assessment.cr-4: Sebuah penelitian rekaan menyurvei 12 karyawan di satu startup Jakarta selama dua minggu, lalu mengklaim bahwa empat hari kerja seminggu 'will work for every company in Indonesia'. Kata mana yang paling tepat menggambarkan penelitian itu? Pilih dari: groundbreaking, uneven, flawed, compelling. Tulis katanya.
assessment.cr-5: Lengkapi kalimat dari sebuah ulasan buku latihan ini dengan SATU kata bahasa Inggris: '___ its middle chapters are slow, the final fifty pages of the novel are among the most moving I have read this year.'
assessment.cr-6: Dr. Wulan mengulas kebijakan rekaan kota Bandung: iuran sampah Rp 50.000 per bulan yang dibayar setiap rumah tangga, kaya atau miskin. Kriterianya: biaya, keadilan dan bukti. Dia menemukan kebijakan itu murah untuk dijalankan dan didukung bukti yang baik dari uji coba di dua kecamatan, tapi iuran itu menyedot bagian yang jauh lebih besar dari penghasilan keluarga miskin. Penilaian akhir mana yang terbaik? A: 'Overall, the policy has some good points and some bad points.' B: 'A low-cost, well-evidenced policy that the council should keep, with a lower fee for low-income households.' C: 'This disastrous policy will ruin poor families and should be scrapped at once.' Tulis A, B atau C.
assessment.cr-7: Lengkapi bagian akhir ulasan latihan tentang sebuah buku panduan rekaan mengenai hukum pajak Indonesia ini dengan SATU kata bahasa Inggris: 'Essential reading for accountants and small-business owners; of ___ interest to general readers.'
